question: What is the main goal of Behavioural Change Communication (BCC) in healthcare?

options.A: To provide complex medical diagnoses to patients
options.C: To promote positive and sustainable health habits
options.D: To document hospital records and supply inventories

explanation: You've got this! BCC uses engaging, interactive communication to help individuals and communities build healthy, lifelong habits. Great job getting familiar with this concept! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h1)

question: How does Behavioural Change Communication (BCC) differ from basic health education?

options.A: BCC focuses on active behavior change rather than just sharing information
options.B: Basic health education involves no communication at all
options.C: BCC is only used inside tertiary hospitals by doctors
options.D: Basic education is meant for children while BCC is for adults

explanation: Think of it this way: health education gives people the facts, but BCC goes a step further to help them actually overcome personal and social barriers to take action. You're building solid community nursing foundations! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h1)

question: Which stage of change describes a person who has not yet considered changing an unhealthy habit?
explanation: In the precontemplation stage, the person isn't even thinking about changing yet, and might not even see that there is a problem. Spotting these stages is a key nursing skill you are mastering easily! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h2)

question: According to the Health Belief Model, what must a patient first believe before changing a health habit?

options.A: They are at personal risk of a serious health problem
options.B: Every member of their village has already changed
options.C: They can afford expensive private hospital care
options.D: The government will pay for all their medical bills

explanation: People rarely change unless they feel vulnerable. The model shows that recognizing personal risk (susceptibility) and the seriousness of the issue must happen first. You are thinking just like a clinical nurse! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h2)

question: The influence of community elders and traditional birth attendants on health choices is an example of which type of determinant?
explanation: Spot on! Cultural norms, traditions, and the advice of respected community elders are classic socio-cultural determinants that shape how people view health. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h3)

question: A nursing mother refuses to take her sick child to the clinic because the nearest facility is across a flooded river with no bridge. What primary factor is affecting her health behaviour?

options.C: An allergic reaction to clinic drugs

explanation: This isn't about her willingness—it's a physical hurdle! Bad roads, long distances, and missing bridges are structural and environmental challenges. You're learning to look at the bigger picture in public health. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h3)

question: Which communication channel is best suited for building deep trust and allowing immediate feedback with a patient?

options.D: A billboard on a major highway

explanation: Nothing beats face-to-face talk! Interpersonal communication lets you clear doubts, answer questions directly, and build wonderful rapport with your patients. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h4)

question: Why are traditional media like village drama troupes and town criers so effective in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: They use familiar cultural formats that local people easily relate to
options.B: They require expensive electricity and satellite dishes
options.C: They are the only legal way to share health messages
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for trained nurses

explanation: Exactly! When you meet people through their own cultural practices like drama and town criers, they naturally tune in and trust the message. Great public health intuition! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h4)

question: What is the main benefit of conducting formative research before launching a community health campaign?

options.A: It proves that foreign health theories are always superior
options.B: It helps nurses understand local beliefs and design appropriate messages
options.C: It eliminates the need to speak the local language
options.D: It guarantees that the government will release extra funds

explanation: Formative research simply means doing your homework on the community first. It helps you design messages that truly fit the people you want to help. You're going to make a brilliant community health nurse! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h5)

question: A nurse wants to promote exclusive breastfeeding in a community where older women traditionally give infants water. What is the most culturally sensitive first step?

options.A: Threaten mothers with heavy fines if they give water to babies
options.B: Engage respected grandmothers to discuss modern infant nutrition benefits
options.C: Ignore the grandmothers and focus only on teenage girls
options.D: Print posters in English warning that local grandmothers are dangerous

explanation: Grandmothers are powerful influencers in our communities! Bringing them on board as allies rather than fighting them is a mark of smart, respectful nursing practice. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h5)

question: Who are considered key stakeholders when mobilizing a Nigerian community for a public health campaign?

options.A: Only the youngest children in the primary school
options.B: Foreign tourists visiting local wildlife parks
options.C: Traditional rulers, religious leaders, and local group heads

explanation: Spot on! Community and religious leaders hold massive influence over public participation. Working with them makes every health campaign smoother. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h6)

question: Why is it important to involve local leaders right from the start of a health project?

options.A: It builds a sense of ownership and encourages community cooperation
options.B: It ensures that only the wealthiest families get treated
options.C: It stops the community from asking questions
options.D: It prevents nurses from having to do any work at all

explanation: When leaders feel involved from day one, they champion the project themselves, leading to wonderful community trust and success! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h6)

question: What type of question is best for encouraging a patient to talk freely during a health counselling session?
explanation: Open-ended questions (like "How do you feel about...?") give clients the floor to share their true thoughts instead of just nodding with a quick yes or no. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h7)

question: Which nursing action demonstrates good interpersonal communication during a patient counselling session?

options.A: Telling the patient their cultural beliefs are completely foolish
options.B: Maintaining an open posture and actively listening without judgment
options.C: Interrupting the patient frequently to speed up the consultation
options.D: Looking strictly at the clinic register while the patient speaks

explanation: Empathy and non-judgmental listening make patients feel safe enough to open up and tell you what's really going on. You're developing great clinical bedside manner! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h7)

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluation in a BCC program?

options.A: Monitoring is done only by doctors, while evaluation is done by patients
options.B: Evaluation happens before the project starts, and monitoring never happens
options.C: There is no difference; both words mean exactly the same thing
options.D: Monitoring is ongoing during the project, while evaluation measures final impact

explanation: Think of monitoring as checking your progress while running the race, and evaluation as looking at your overall performance and medals when the race is finished. You've got this distinction down! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h8)

question: A nurse leading a polio vaccination campaign notices sudden community resistance due to false rumors spread on social media. What is the best immediate response?

options.A: Punish any community member who asks questions about the vaccine
options.B: Engage trusted community leaders to openly address and debunk the rumors
options.C: Ignore the rumors completely and hope the villagers forget them
options.D: Cancel the entire vaccination campaign and close the health clinic

explanation: Rumors spread fast, but trusted local voices spread clarity faster! Partnering with community leaders is the best way to calm fears and protect public health. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h8)
